name: Icon
purpose: Normalize one consumer-authored SVG with Brick sizing, semantic foreground, alignment, direction, and decorative-or-informative accessibility semantics.
useWhen: An authored SVG needs Brick size, currentColor-based tone, alignment, or opt-in directional RTL mirroring.

avoidWhen.condition: The graphic performs an action or needs its own touch target.
avoidWhen.useInstead: Button, IconButton, Toggle, or the owning interactive component

avoidWhen.condition: The content is a photo, raster asset, responsive media object, fallback, or loading state.
The graphic is a logo, illustration, chart, or multiregion visual with independent semantics.
avoidWhen.useInstead: an application-owned SVG or media composition with explicit semantics

composition: Pass exactly one consumer-authored SVG element; prefer the default span wrapper and use asChild only when the direct root must remain that SVG.
When visible nearby text already provides the meaning, keep Icon decorative; when a standalone icon conveys information, provide label or aria-labelledby.
Inside an icon-only control, label the control and leave its nested Icon decorative.
Use createIcon at module scope for reusable authored geometry and an SVGSVGElement ref; choose exactly one d or path, retaining fixed authored fills.
Let Button/IconButton own artwork dimensions; no redundant Icon size is needed, and explicit semantic tone remains available.

rules.statement: Use Icon only for visual content; never use it as an interactive host or touch target.
Keep the decorative default when meaning is redundant, or provide exactly one nonempty label or aria-labelledby reference when the standalone graphic is informative.
Give an icon-only Button, IconButton, Toggle, or other control its accessible name on the control, not on its nested Icon.
Use currentColor for single-color SVG fills or strokes so Brick tone and inherited control state can apply.
Choose the semantic palette with tone and choose readable text paint versus stronger solid paint with emphasis; do not encode a compound palette name or use paint as the only carrier of meaning.
Enable directional only for glyphs whose meaning reverses in RTL, such as arrows and forward/back controls.
Use asChild only with one direct non-interactive SVG; never compose Icon onto a button, anchor, input, or other interactive host.

Use Center, Square, or Circle when an icon needs two-axis centering or invariant equal-size geometry; compose Surface for its paint. Use Stack or an owning component icon slot for sibling alignment instead of wrapper spans or application offsets.
Load styles.css or core.css plus icon.css.

Presentation resolves instance > nearest provider > factory > library. IconPropsProvider accepts only size, tone and emphasis; undefined inherits outer properties and responsive sizes replace whole values.
Use ResponsiveIconSize with initial/sm/md/lg/xl. Sparse values start at md, omitted breakpoints retain the last active value, and inherit follows typography outside action slots.

Use one noninteractive SVG for asChild. Atom composeHost preserves both refs, React 19 callback cleanup, child class/style and owner-first events; default prevention does not suppress the child handler. Owner naming wins.
Icon and its provider consume client context and support React SSR/hydration. Define createIcon calls in client modules in RSC applications; do not claim server-only factory execution.
Factory defaults never carry contextual names, refs or host substitution. Name each informative instance using label or aria-labelledby; factory output is exactly one SVG.
Directional mirroring follows effective :dir(rtl), including nested LTR. Independent scale composes with authored transforms; do not mirror both SVG and wrapper.

commonMistakes.mistake: Using a raw SVG with ad hoc width, color, alignment, or ARIA inside ordinary Brick composition.
commonMistakes.correction: Wrap the authored SVG in Icon, choose the semantic size/tone recipe, and let the owning Stack or control align it.

commonMistakes.mistake: Giving both the control and its nested Icon the same accessible label.
commonMistakes.correction: Label the control and keep the nested Icon decorative to prevent duplicate announcements.

commonMistakes.mistake: Using directional on logos, status symbols, checks, clocks, or other glyphs that do not reverse meaning in RTL.
commonMistakes.correction: Leave directional false unless the glyph itself communicates direction.

validation: Check decorative and informative accessibility trees, icon-only control naming, all sizes, tones, and emphases, currentColor adoption, flex shrinking, and RTL directional mirroring.
Confirm asChild targets only one SVG and that CSS is present.
Verify React 18/19 refs, StrictMode cleanup, SSR/hydration, responsive md/inherit restoration, provider/factory precedence and all seven action-slot sizes.
